dataset_metadata.description: GovReport is a large-scale dataset for long-document summarization consisting of reports published by the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) and the Congressional Research Service (CRS). It is characterized by significantly longer documents and summaries compared to standard datasets like CNN/DailyMail, requiring models to handle high-complexity administrative and policy-oriented language.

schema_analysis.description: The full body text of the government report, containing detailed policy analysis and data.
An expert-written executive summary of the report, serving as the target for abstractive summarization.

structural_logic.relationships: The 'report' column acts as the source input representing a long-form discourse, while 'summary' is the ground-truth condensed representation of the key findings and recommendations.
structural_logic.label_dynamics: Extremely high compression ratio (approx. 17:1); summaries are much longer and more structurally complex than typical news summaries, often containing multiple paragraphs.
structural_logic.potential_bottlenecks: The extreme document length (frequently exceeding 10,000 tokens) poses a major bottleneck for standard self-attention mechanisms; the formal, bureaucratic vocabulary requires domain-specific understanding.
